vectors.description: worked numbers: E1 = 10 + ceilDiv(40,960, 100,000) = 11, E5 = 5,000, outTokEst = 300, E7 = 14,950: predicted = 19,961 ms
an honest peer finishing at elapsed 20,500: ratio 973
a peer whose truth is half its claim: elapsed = 11 + 10,000 + 29,900 = 39,911, ratio 500
burst at the end: first chunk at tBody + 50, all the rest in one chunk just before tEnd: the same ratio as evenly spaced chunks (973)
split chunks: the same 1,200 bytes as 300 chunks: identical outBytes and ratio
split chunks: the same 1,200 bytes one byte per chunk: identical outBytes and ratio
merged chunks: the same text in 2 chunks: identical ratio
a lying INFER_END adds usage, ttftMs, totalMs and token counts claiming 10x speed: the members are ignored, the ratio is unchanged (973)
a late INFER_HEAD (5 s after content began): no effect, the head's time is unused
reported heat: st.tb = 2 on every piggyback has no effect on predicted (claim row only)
reported queue: qb = 2 on every piggyback: no discard, the ratio is unchanged

padding under the cap: 3,000 bytes (1,200 real + 1,800 filler) in the honest time: outTokEst 750, E7 = 37,450, predicted 42,461, ratio 2,071 (placement still cannot exceed the claim: effRatio = min(1000, ...))
padding over the cap: 8,193 bytes at maxTokens 1,024 (cap 8,192): DISCARD_OVERLONG
padding exactly at the cap (8,192 bytes) is kept: this is the worst case that the tracker cannot see (R3-OVERCLAIM-1)
settings switch: INFER_ACCEPT.fileSha256 differs from the claim key: DISCARD_SETTINGS
settings switch: the engine backend this requester holds for the peer differs from the claim row's
settings switch: the engine commit differs from the claim row's
another attempt of this requester was in flight on that peer: DISCARD_CONCURRENT
the attempt did not end with terminal = done: DISCARD_INCOMPLETE
127 bytes is SHORT; 128 is kept (SHORT_BYTES = 128)
128 bytes is kept
discard order: INCOMPLETE outranks SHORT, OVERLONG, CONCURRENT and SETTINGS
discard order: OVERLONG outranks CONCURRENT and SETTINGS
discard order: CONCURRENT outranks SETTINGS
a very fast peer: the ratio is capped at RATIO_CAP = 5,000
a zero elapsed time is treated as 1 ms (checked arithmetic)
tEnd is the LATER of INFER_END and the last chunk (a chunk after the end frame counts)
the claim's throttle onset is honoured by the prediction (onset 5,000 ms: coolMs at the decode rate, the rest at the steady rate)
5 kept observations of the half-speed peer: state DISCREPANT, and its placement is min(1000, median 500) = its true speed (prefill 50,000, decode 10,000)
4 kept observations are UNVERIFIED whatever the ratios (MIN_STATE = 5)
n = 0: prior' = claim x 700 / 1000 (prefill 70,000, decode 14,000)
n = 1: the blend (2 x prior' + claim x min(1000, x)) / 3
n = 2: the blend with two kept ratios
n = 3: the lower median of the kept ratios, capped at 1000
an even n takes the lower median x[(n - 1) / 2]: n = 6
an honest busy peer (queueing on 2 of 5): ratios {400, 450, 900, 950, 960}: best = x[3] = 950 -> CORROBORATED, placement min(1000, x[2] = 900)
a fast peer: every ratio above 1000 still places at the claim (effRatio = min(1000, median))
best = x[(3n)/4]: the upper quartile of 5 ratios is x[3]
truncation: four answers of < 128 bytes: the discard budget trips at the 4th, state WEAK, tracked rate clamped to the lowest ratio among observations of >= 8 bytes
truncation with every answer under 8 bytes: no qualifying observation, the tracked rate clamps to 0 (the candidate then fails F8)
exactly half discarded (2 of 4) does not trip the budget
more than half discarded (3 of 5) trips the budget even with kept ratios
the window keeps the last WIN = 20 kept ratios (25 observations)
R3-OVERCLAIM-1: a peer truly 5x slower than it claims, padding every answer to the cap (8,192 bytes), reads CORROBORATED and is placed at the full claim
the same padding against a peer only 7x slower: WEAK (the residual is bounded, not absent)
OVERLONG answers add a strike each and are never kept
a concurrent attempt is discarded and does not enter the window
state thresholds: best = 800 is CORROBORATED
state thresholds: best = 799 is WEAK
state thresholds: best = 600 is WEAK
state thresholds: best = 599 is DISCREPANT
the peer-wide 400 permille discount replaces 700 (n = 0: prefill 40,000)
capRef below the claim binds prior' while n < 3: min(claim, capRef) x 700 / 1000 (prefill 35,000)
capRef does not apply once n >= 3 (the observed median replaces the prior)
an inherited DISCREPANT state stays DISCREPANT whatever the new ratios say until it clears
ratios above 1000 in the window: the median is capped, the state uses the raw best
a WEAK budget clamp never lifts a lower tracked rate: min(median-based, minRatio-based)
the peer publishes a new claim seq twice in one day: the second is ignored for routing until 24 h pass
a claim body with a seq that is not higher is never accepted (rollback)
